name: Lili Vadi Kathiyavadi Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Kathiyawadi thali joint locals point to in Patan town — walking distance from most of the Patan hotel cluster, ~15 min from Rani-ki-Vav. The thali is the meal most temple/heritage visitors get post-visit. Kathiyawadi (spicier, less sweet) vs the mainland Gujarati style; closer to what rural Patan-Mehsana belt households cook.
insider_tip: Lunch is the right meal (12-3pm); dinner repeats thinner. The rotla + lasaniya batata is the Kathiyawadi-specific combo worth ordering even if you skip the full thali. Cash and UPI both work; AC sit-down available.

name: Apple Residency Restaurant
why_it_matters: Apple Residency is a 3-star hotel a 10-minute drive from Rani-ki-Vav — the in-house restaurant is one of the few AC sit-downs in Patan. Multi-cuisine but the Gujarati side is the strongest. Cooked-to-order breakfast 7-11am for hotel guests; lunch and dinner for both guests and walk-ins. Wins for travellers staying overnight in Patan who want a calmer dinner than the Vardhaman Nagar bazaar restaurants.
insider_tip: Breakfast (if staying) is the most consistent meal. Skip the Indo-Chinese section. Walk-ins are fine for lunch and dinner — the restaurant accepts non-guests without fuss.
signature_address: Apple Residency, Near Pakwan Road, Patan, Gujarat 384265

name: The Grand Raveta Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Grand Raveta is a Patan hotel 1 minute from Sahasralinga Talav and 7 minutes from Rani-ki-Vav — newer property, the cleanest in-Patan-town restaurant for travellers visiting both the stepwell and the Sahasralinga reservoir. Standard hotel multi-cuisine; Gujarati thali is the order most heritage-tourists default to.
insider_tip: Reservation matters during the November-February tourist peak. The thali is fine but not exceptional; Lili Vadi delivers more authentic Kathiyawadi at half the price. Stay here only if you need a hotel base, not a destination meal.
signature_address: The Grand Raveta, Near Sahasralinga Talav, Patan, Gujarat 384265
